For negative bar count and large values, we need mock BarSeries to return custom counts. Use Mockito to mock BarSeries and stub getBarCount().

For exception case, stub getBarCount() to throw RuntimeException.

For null BarSeries case, we construct CashFlow with null and expect NullPointerException when getSize() called.

We'll use Mockito for zero as well.

Simpler: Use Mockito.mock(BarSeries.class) for all cases, stub getBarCount().

If not, we can simulate by creating new series with 6 bars.

Simplify: Use mock that returns 5 then after adding bar we stub to return 6. But we need to test that getSize reflects updated count. Could use a spy on a real series and change stub.

Given limited knowledge, we can use Mockito to create a mock BarSeries that returns 5 initially, then after we call some method we change stub to 6 before calling getSize. The description: "After creating a BarSeries with 5 bars, adding one more bar should cause getSize() to reflect the updated count (6)." So we can simulate by creating a mock that initially returns 5, then we call series.addBar(...). We'll need to stub addBar to change internal count. Simpler: Use a mutable integer array to store count and have getBarCount() return that value; after adding bar we increment.

Better: Use Mockito with Answer that reads from AtomicInteger count.

```

BarSeries series = mock(BarSeries.class);
when(series.getBarCount()).thenAnswer(invocation -> count.get());
doAnswer(invocation -> { count.incrementAndGet(); return null; }).when(series).addBar(any());

Assuming BarSeries has addBar method; not sure but we can just call count.incrementAndGet() manually in test without invoking series.addBar.
